correctness.rationale: The Boolean idempotents recover the underlying points; singleton products recover every partial bijection, so all automorphisms are conjugations. The existence of each two-point bijection recovers equality of positive distances, not their names. On a cycle the image of the distance-one class must itself be a connected cycle; a step k generates the vertex group, and the edge isomorphism is forced by the image of 0 and of 1. The even antipodal class is a disconnected matching and n=3 has just one class. For n>=5 a wheel has two classes; the complement has maximum degree n-3 rather than n, so there is no class swap. The unique hub is fixed and the rim is dihedral. These structural arguments settle all sizes regardless of the supplied finite test bounds.
residual_risks: The supplied finite verifier tests vertex normalizers, not arbitrary monoid self-bijections; correctness of spatiality is established separately by the argument.

evidence: Corollary 6.5 recovers an ordinary graph up to complement from its abstract PAut. Its proof uses rank-one idempotents, singleton arrows and ranks up to two to identify the specific vertex bijection, not just abstract existence.

evidence: All elements of the cycle monoid are restrictions of its units D_{2n}, so its spatial normalizer is exactly the normalizer of the units. The rotation group is generated by the elements of order n (n>=3), hence characteristic. A permutation normalizing it has form x↦a+ux, u a unit. Every such map conjugates a reflection into a reflection and normalizes D_{2n}.
For a wheel the complement option in Corollary 6.5 is impossible by the hub degree; all remaining permutations restrict to usual rim symmetries.

evidence: A complete graph with each pair colored by its distance gives the identical partial-isometry monoid under color-preserving partial graph automorphisms. Rank-two existence recovers same-color pairs.
A diameter-two graph such as a wheel has the same partial isometries as partial automorphisms of its induced subgraphs; the cycle monoid instead equals all restrictions of the dihedral action.

originality.rationale: The exact graph-specific formulas are not printed together in the sources checked, but their abstract monoid conclusions are routine consequences of published stronger descriptions, not merely similarities of titles or groups. In particular the proof of Jajcay et al. Corollary 6.5 recovers the underlying bijection from the monoid isomorphism, identifies rank-two restrictions and recovers the graph up to complement on that same bijection. The wheel metric monoid is PAut(W_n), so the wheel result specializes this proof with the degree obstruction to self-complementarity. The colored-graph monoid framework already has the same rank-two data as the general metric result. For cycles, the older dihedral-restriction lemma and spatiality reduce the answer to the ordinary permutation normalizer of D_{2n}; its rotation subgroup is characteristic and its normalizer is the usual cyclic holomorph. This is positive coverage by implication, not a failure based on retrieval limits.
residual_risks: No earlier paper inspected was found printing both formulas side by side. The decision is based on explicit implication from inspected sources, not a claim about the first printed wording.

One normalizes a known action generated by rotations and reflections, and the other is the immediate non-self-complementary graph case of rank-two reconstruction.
